newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Whitbread favoured by consumer glee.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Whitbread favoured by consumer glee.

text.p: British brewer to hotels group Whitbread Plc is expected to report a near 12 percent increase in its full year profits on Wednesday, driven by a background of strong consumer demand, said analysts.

"The profits growth will come mainly from their retail side which has benefited from a combination of acquisitions and a pick up in the South of England where their core strengths are," said Dermot Carr, analyst at Nikko.
Analysts forecasts for pretax profits range from 313 to 321 million stg, up from 285.7 million last time. A dividend of 23.8p per share is expected, an increase from 21.85 last time.

Whitbread is banking on the fact that, although the trend for eating out is rising, the average British consumer spends about one fifth of their total food spend on eating out compared with half in the United States.

The economic background of relatively low and stable inflation and interest rates has helped whip up more consumer confidence which will feed through into increased sales at Whitbread's managed pubs as well as occupancy rates at Marriott hotels, said analysts.

"Whitbread's policy of investing in its hotels, pubs and leisure assets in the last few years when the consumer environment has been picking up will translate into strong profits growth because the cost of borrowing is much lower than the return on that investment," said Lehman Brothers analyst Fraser Ramzan.

The company has spent about 300 million stg on a combination of buying the Pelican chain of restaurants, and expanding its chain of pub-restaurants Brewers Fayre and sports clubs David Lloyd Leisure in the year to March 1997.
Also in the development pipeline are 45 Travel Inns, 80 managed pubs, and 40 Costa Coffee outlets.
Whitbread shares set a high of 820 for the year and a low of 729p. The shares stood at 767-1/2p, down 1p at 1213 GMT.
